subject: design/worktracker-hierarchy-index
statement: the reverse edge is maintained **incrementally** at the base store's single edge-mutation choke point (`create`, `setParent`, `clearParent`), under the child's existing per-item lock, writing the item first and then creating/removing exactly one marker (DINV-5). Recovery is a **full `reindex`** — a pure O(N) rebuild from the item `parent` fields — run lazily on first use when `rev/` is absent, on a detected mismatch, and when a cheap dirty check trips (the hand-edit case, NR-2); it is the only drift-recovery (DINV-6). This split is deliberate and measured: the incremental write is orders of magnitude cheaper than a rebuild, so rebuild-on-write is rejected (it would blow the interactive/scheduling bound and go quadratic on bulk creation — `design-brainstorm:worktracker-hierarchy-query-tech-design#D-5`), while a full rebuild is cheap enough at the store's capacity target to be the *sole* recovery, which deletes a whole class of self-healing logic.
